field_001: How Wayland Chin helped modernize a university English assessment workflow through ZipGrade-supported marking, exam formatting, and aligned revision lessons.
field_005: Using automation for repetitive objective marking while preserving professional judgment for speaking, writing, and feedback.
field_007: Multiple-choice examinations created a large volume of repetitive hand-marking. At the same time, students needed practice materials that reflected the structure and language demands of the assessment without reproducing live exam content.
field_008: The opportunity was not to automate assessment indiscriminately. It was to separate objective handling from work that requires a teacher’s interpretation, then improve each part of the process.
field_016: I advocated for the use of ZipGrade and bubble-sheet responses for objective Pre-Intermediate examinations. I also provide feedback on exam formatting and develop review or revision lessons based on the assessment structure.
field_018: The programme coordinator is responsible for creating the examinations. My contribution is workflow improvement, formatting support, feedback, and the development of aligned revision materials.
field_022: The responsible colleague creates the programme examination.
field_025: Objective responses are arranged for clear bubble-sheet capture.
field_028: ZipGrade checks multiple-choice responses without manual item-by-item marking.
field_031: Teachers retain responsibility for tasks that require professional judgment.
field_034: Revision lessons reinforce the language, skills, and task types students will need.
field_036: The programme’s final, team-accessible materials show two complementary outputs: a Pre-Intermediate practice examination in the same format as the formal assessment, and a multi-stage final-exam review unit. The public examples below are reconstructed to demonstrate the workflow without revealing current exam questions or answer keys.
field_045: Multiple-choice responses can be captured consistently, removing repetitive hand-checking from the teacher’s workload.
field_054: The review unit gives students structured practice in the relevant skills while keeping live assessment materials confidential.
field_056: Teacher time is redirected: less repetitive objective marking, with more attention available for qualitative work.
field_057: Formatting becomes functional: clear layouts support scanning, administration, and student use.
field_058: Preparation stays aligned: review materials connect classroom practice to assessment expectations.
field_059: Automation remains selective: technology supports the process without replacing teacher judgment.
field_061: ZipGrade is currently used for objective examinations at the Pre-Intermediate level. Broader use across the programme has been discussed, but this case study does not present that expansion as completed.
field_063: Assessment modernization does not require automating everything. A stronger design identifies which tasks are repetitive and rules-based, then protects teacher time for the work that depends on observation, interpretation, and meaningful feedback.
field_065: No student records, live exam questions, answer keys, or confidential results are displayed in this case study.
field_070: Use technology for repetitive objective work and preserve teacher expertise for interpretation and feedback.
